options.text: Saliva breaks starch in the chapati into sugar, so the chewed chapati gives a weaker blue-black iodine colour than the unchewed chapati.
Unchewed chapati also gives little or no blue-black colour with iodine.
Saliva changes sugar into starch, so iodine turns darker after chewing.
Saliva changes the protein in egg white into sugar.

stem:
Aarav chews a piece of plain chapati for about one minute. It begins to taste sweet. He places iodine on unchewed chapati and on the chewed chapati. He also has egg white as a protein food that is not starch. Iodine can give a blue-black colour with starch.

Which claim is correct?

teacher.key_rationale: Saliva acts on starch in chapati to form sugar, so sweetness rises and the iodine starch colour weakens after chewing. Unchewed chapati still has starch; saliva does not reverse sugar to starch or digest egg-white protein into sugar.
